Transcribed from the PROVENANCE header of jl4/examples/legal/bna/source-s1.txt (PR #195, unmerged at this writing), so the local paths point forward and the digest checks report `skip` on branches where that file is absent. in_force.statement: British Nationality Act 1981, Section 1 is up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 04 July 2026. There are changes that may be brought into force at a future date.

assembled.note: The provenance-headed artifact P3 encodes from: the verbatim s 1 text with its F/C annotation lists, plus a s 50 definitional annex. This is the only digest in the bundle that pins bytes we hold, which is why the schema keeps it separate from the retrieved documents.

documents.title: British Nationality Act 1981, section 1 — Acquisition by birth or adoption (legislation.gov.uk revised text)

integrity.sha256_absent_reason: Direct retrieval was blocked by an AWS WAF JavaScript challenge (HTTP 202, x-amzn-waf-action: challenge) for both curl and WebFetch, so the bytes came from a Wayback capture we do not hold. The capture is immutable and pinned by its timestamp; the digest that is checkable is the assembled artifact's.

annotations.inventory_note: legislation.gov.uk's inline textual-amendment markers, resolved in the "Textual Amendments" list printed below the section. Preserved because P2 disposes over them and P5 joins on that disposition table — the words alone would not have carried the inventory.

The "Modifications etc. (not altering text)" list. Completeness is asserted here precisely because the hand sweep dropped C2 (SMOKE-REPORT.md §3.5); declaring the inventory complete is what turns the cross-file disposition check on.
